Use richer user-goal signals, not just clicks, to model why users choose items and align recommendations with those goals. [1, 2, 4, 9] Papers propose using explicit context feedback, review text, and natural-language profiles to capture semantic reasons behind preferences, which can make recommendations more personalized, transparent, and steerable. [1, 2, 9]

Another approach is to infer and use high-level intents or motivations during reasoning, so the system can understand intrinsic behavior patterns and stay robust to noisy interactions. [2, 4, 10] One paper also argues for semantic profiles built from LLMs and knowledge graphs to better represent preferences and propagate them in recommendation models. [3]
